I've been farming this land for over 30 years, same as my father before me. In Quzhou, there's really only one rotation that makes sense: winter wheat, then summer corn on the same ground. That's what everyone does, that's what the land is suited for, and that's what the grain buyers expect. I have 12 mu in total.

For wheat, I'll till the soil with the rotary machine before planting in October — I've tried no-till on wheat and the emergence was uneven. I'll use a Shimai or Hengguan improved variety, not seeds I saved myself, because the certified stuff yields better and I've seen that firsthand. I apply compound fertilizer (磷酸二铵 + 氯化钾) as a base before sowing, then top-dress urea at jointing stage. I water three times: once before sowing to settle moisture, once at jointing, once at heading. I know the researchers at the station say two irrigations is enough, but I'm not willing to risk a dry heading period and lose half the yield. Two pesticide rounds: herbicide in late winter, then an aphid/fungicide spray in April when things warm up.

For maize, I plant directly into the wheat stubble — no tillage, just seed into the ground. I use a hybrid like Zhengdan 958, which I trust. Summer rain usually carries most of the water need, so I only irrigate once unless it turns dry in August. One herbicide pass after emergence, one borer spray in July. Fertilizer is front-loaded as compound base, then urea at big bell stage.
